call_points.text: Company expects to realize ₹40 to ₹50 Cr of subsidies from Odisha in FY27 across wage, power, and capex heads.
Management aims to sustain double-digit volume growth momentum into the new fiscal year.
E-commerce now contributes 15% of total revenue, gaining a couple of percentage points YoY.
Marketing spend was a little over 4% of sales in FY26 and is targeted to rise to close to 5% in FY27.
Production efficiency margin expansion potential remains as Odisha and K.R. Pet plants mature from current suboptimal levels.
Targeting Rs. 8,000 Cr in revenue by FY29, driven by modernised retail, expanded channels, and consumer demand.
Cotton and key input cost inflation persists; managed through strategic sourcing, supply chain efficiencies, and calibrated pricing.
Network spans 1,15,644 MBOs, 1,579 EBS, and 893 Large Format Stores across 2,731 cities & towns.

operating_notes.text: 64% in-house manufacturing across 16 units with 280 million pieces production capacity.
Inventory days stood at 73 days at end of Q4FY26 vs 64 days at start of year; net working capital days at 56 days vs 54 days.
Store network comprised 116,600+ MBOs, 1,615 EBOs, and 893 LFS as of Q4FY26.
Sales volume was 61.9 million pieces in Q1FY27, up 5.7% YoY, with about three days of invoiced billing undelivered at quarter-end.
A 2.2% weighted average price increase was taken in May 2026, after 2.5% in January 2026; the May increase was linked to raw material cost.
Distribution stood at 115,871 multi-brand outlets, 1,640 exclusive brand stores and 930 large format stores; online is over 35% of the Speedo business.

timeline.summary: Q4FY26 results (standalone): revenue ₹1,252.6 Cr (+14.1% YoY), net profit ₹178.73 Cr (+9.0% YoY).
Page Industries released its Q4FY26 presentation targeting ₹8,000 Cr revenue by FY29 and reporting Q4 volume growth of 10.8% YoY.
Page Industries Limited shared the audio recording link for its Q4FY26 and FY26 results investor call on May 21, 2026.
Page Industries guided FY27 EBITDA margins of 19-21%, flagged a Q1 price hike for RM inflation, and guided ₹40-50 Cr in Odisha subsidies.
Page Industries' Q1FY27 call (13 Aug 2026) reported revenue up 7.9% to ₹1,420 Cr and PAT down 4% to ₹193 Cr, with EBITDA margin at 20.3% and FY27 margin guidance held at 19-21%.
Page Industries and Yellow Flower Trading LLC filed separate appeals in Dubai Court following the court's dismissal of YFT's claim.

watchlist.response: Said the garmenting wage revision was already actioned in April and is in the P&L; the May announcement excludes garmenting and has no material impact, and was withheld by the state in late July. Did not give a number for a garmenting-inclusive hike.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked what margin impact a 60% Karnataka minimum wage hike would have if garmenting were included.

watchlist.response: Said it is very difficult to put a number given volatility, and that the increase only partially covers input costs.
watchlist.text: Analyst pressed on how much of the raw material inflation the May price hike offsets.

watchlist.response: Declined to quantify exactly, saying roughly three days of billing went undelivered versus the usual three to four days.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the quantum of undelivered volume from logistics disruption.

watchlist.response: Said secondary numbers are not disclosed, but secondary growth was much better than primary.
watchlist.text: Analyst asked for the gap between primary and secondary growth.
